newsitem.title: USA: Texas A&M $64 mln sale waits for better rates.
newsitem.headline: Texas A&M $64 mln sale waits for better rates.

text.p: When will interest rates go lower? For the Texas A&M University System Board of Regents, that's the $64 million question.
"We're about 25 basis points away from where we want to see rates overall," said Gregory Anderson, assistant vice chancellor and treasurer at the university system.

From the standpoint of the U.S. Treasury's 30-year bond, the benchmark would need to be closer to 6.60 percent for the deal to arrive, he said. The bond was yielding 7.17 percent around midday Monday.

University system officials began contemplating the offering in November, and the system's board approved it in January, Anderson said. The offering received Texas Bond Review Board approval on February 20.
"We actually weren't ready to go until the first week in March, and that's when rates really started going up," he said. "It's been kind of a downhill slide since then."
The proposed $64 million sale breaks down to $8 million of refunding bonds, a $40 million conversion from commercial paper into fixed-rate bonds, and $16 million of new money, Anderson said.
The new money portion will be used for classroom facilities at campuses in Laredo, Kingsville and Corpus Christi.
